chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, he said: Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin narrated to me, saying: I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man who emits madhy while he is in salat, whether from desire or from other than desire.
He عليه السلام said: From madhy there is wudu (ablution).

His statement عليه السلام, 'From madhy there is wudu,' may be understood as an expression of astonishment regarding it, as though because of the well-known and evident ruling of not repeating wudu because of it, he said: 'Is this something from which wudu is performed?' It is also possible that it may be understood as a form of taqiyyah, because that is the doctrine of most of the 'ammah.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: taqiyyah, dissimulation or precautionary conformity mentioned as a possible explanation
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the state in which the emission occurs
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni public or majority, whose view is referenced in the explanation
key_terms.الْمَذْيُ: pre-seminal fluid discussed here as a subject of ritual purity rulings
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification mentioned in the report
key_terms.شَهْوَةٍ: desire, one possible cause of the emission mentioned in the question

ai.seo_question: Does emitting madhy during salat require wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of madhy emitted during salat, whether caused by desire or not. The apparent wording indicates wudu, while the compiler explains that it may be interpreted differently or attributed to taqiyyah due to the view held by most of the 'ammah.
